additions.reason: The source text opens with the concept of ruach shtut as the central antagonist ('לְגָרֵשׁ מִקִּרְבּוֹ הָרוּחַ שְׁטוּת, מַה שֶּׁלִּבּוֹ מָלֵא מֵרוּחַ שְׁטוּת הַדָּבוּק בּוֹ'), and paragraph 2 explicitly declares its nature: 'הָרוּחַ הוּא הָאֲוִיר' — making ruach shtut identical in nature to avir (air). This is a bechina-language identity statement. Ruach shtut exists in the dataset as a node (it appears in Torah #1 Package 3 and its edge 14943 in the broader dataset), confirming it is a recognized concept. However, there is no bechina edge for ruach shtut under reference 176. A new bechina edge should be added: ruach shtut ↔ avir (ref 176).

additions.reason: Paragraph 2 of the source text states: 'הָרוּחַ הוּא הָאֲוִיר, וְטֶבַע הָאֲוִיר לְבַקֵּשׁ לוֹ מָקוֹם פָּנוּי לָצֵאת שָׁם' — the spirit IS the air, and the nature of air is to seek an empty space to escape through. The Rebbe uses avir (air) not as a metaphor but as the actual physical identity of ruach shtut, explaining its mechanism of movement and displacement. This is a bechina-equivalent identity, not a causal statement. The avir node does not appear in the current dataset for ref 176 as either a bechina or eitza node — it is a genuine gap. It should be added as the second node in the ruach shtut bechina pair.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: לב הצדיק חלל (the Tzaddik's heart as hollow/empty)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Paragraph 2 says 'וְלֵב הַצַּדִּיק הוּא חָלָל, בִּבְחִינַת: וְלִבִּי חָלַל בְּקִרְבִּי'. The word בִּבְחִינַת here introduces a scriptural proof-text (Tehillim 109), not a conceptual bechina equivalence. The Rebbe is citing the verse as evidence that the Tzaddik's heart has the quality of chalal (hollow), not establishing chalal as a bechina-equivalent concept node distinct from lev haTzaddik. The chalal is a property of the Tzaddik's heart used to explain the physical mechanism, not a parallel-identity concept. Excluded.

Paragraph 2 describes the ruach/avir seeking 'מָקוֹם פָּנוּי' (an empty space) to escape through — this is a functional description of the mechanism, not a bechina declaration. The text says the avir seeks such a place; it does not state that makom panui IS a bechina of any other concept. The empty space is the chalal of the Tzaddik's heart, which functions as a destination in the causal chain. No bechina-language marker accompanies this concept. Excluded.

Paragraph 1 defines hitkashrut (connection) as 'אַהֲבַת נֶפֶשׁ' — 'that is, soul-love for the Tzaddik.' This uses 'הַיְנוּ' (that is, meaning), which could signal a bechina equivalence. However, in context this is a definitional gloss — the Rebbe is explaining what hitkashrut means rather than declaring two independent concepts to share the same essential nature. Hitkashrut and ahavat nefesh are presented as the same act described differently (one is the abstract form, one is the content), but they function as a single eitza node in the dataset (edge 2067 uses the compound: 'שֶׁנִּתְקַשֵּׁר לְהַצַּדִּיק הָאֱמֶת, וְהִתְקַשְּׁרוּת הַיְנוּ אַהֲבַת נֶפֶשׁ' as a SINGLE node1_id). The dataset has already collapsed these into one compound node, which is correct. Excluded as a new bechina addition — it is already one node.

Paragraph 2 uses 'הוּא בּוֹקֵעַ וְשׁוֹבֵר בִּמְהִירוּת וּבְבֶהָלָה' as a description of the physical behavior of air/ruach shtut. This is a characterization of how the spirit acts, not a declaration of bechina-equivalence with another concept. Excluded.

Lev nishbar appears as a node in the dataset (edge 1551, node2_id) but only in an eitza edge — it is the RESULT of expelling ruach shtut quickly. There is no bechina-language statement equating lev nishbar to any parallel concept in Torah #176. The source text says 'עַל־יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ לוֹ לֵב נִשְׁבָּר' (through this HE HAS a broken heart) — a causal statement. Excluded from bechina package analysis.
